# Phase 10 action 4.4 — upper-bound archetype pilots (session 2 of 2)

CHECKPOINT-PHASE10.md 4.4: *"per-archetype random-init pilots trained to
convergence (7c rec #4) — lifts the D0-piloted matrix caveat and
supplies gated-league pressure at the top."*

This session's three decks: **M3BlueSkies**, **M3RedRush**,
**M3GreenRamp**. (Sibling session covers the other three.)

*Results tables are generated by `rl/p10_pilots_report.py`; this file is
written as the runs land.*

## Why this run exists

The 7c robustness matrix rated every archetype row with a **D0 pilot**,
and `p7c_pilot_calib.sh` then showed D0 is not a neutral instrument.
Its screen B (D1 vs D0, same deck both seats, 100g) reads:

| deck | D1 over D0 |
|---|---|
| dimir | .62 |
| ramp | .58 |
| redrush | **.44** |
| skies | **.43** |

On two of this session's three decks the *search* seat is a **worse**
pilot than the heuristic one — the scripted ladder is inverted off the
mirror, exactly the caveat CHECKPOINT-PHASE10.md section 6 records. So
"the agent beats archetype X at .87" has never been a statement about
X's ceiling; it is a statement about a pilot of unknown, deck-dependent
competence. A learned pilot trained on the deck itself is the missing
instrument.

## Method

Recipe, identical for all three decks:

- **From random init.** All three start from `rl_p7_scratch_init.pt` —
  the same random-init lstmattn that Phase 7b's scratch line started
  from — so deck is the only variable between the three pilots, and the
  p7b curve is a legitimate reference line.
- **The agent pilots the archetype** (`-Drl.deck`), and every pool row
  carries its own deck (`-Drl.oppDeck`, the 7c pool schema).
- **PFSP league** (`rl/p10_pilot_lane.sh`, fork of `league_lane_p7.sh`),
  optimistic Elo selection targeting ~100 Elo above the agent's current
  rating. Pool = the **field** these pilots exist to pressure
  (D0/D1/D1h + ck_6144 + attn_desp + p7c ck_1536, all on BenchDimir)
  plus the lane's **own snapshots** on the archetype deck as the low
  ladder rungs a from-scratch net needs.
- **Rating every 2048 episodes**: 100g vs **D0 piloting BenchDimir** —
  the 7c matrix cell with the seats swapped.
- **200g vs ck_6144** (the project champion, on BenchDimir) at the end
  of each pilot.
- Fast path throughout (persistent driver JVM); training chunks
  concurrent, **every rating and every champion match sequential**.

### Reading the rating: deck power is divided out

Raw win rate vs D0-BenchDimir conflates deck strength with pilot skill,
and these decks are not equal to BenchDimir. `p7c_pilot_calib.sh`
screen A (D0 on deck X vs D0 on BenchDimir, 100g) measured:

| deck | power | note |
|---|---|---|
| skies | .71 | |
| redrush | .64 | |
| ramp | .60 | |
| dimir | .58 | same-deck seat baseline — this is what "no deck edge" reads |

so the curve also reports a normalised pseudo-Elo

    elo = 1000 + 400*log10(wr/(1-wr)) - 400*log10(power/(1-power))
               + 400*log10(.58/.42)

on which **a pilot exactly as good as D0 scores ~1000** whatever it is
piloting, i.e. the same scale as the mirror Elo ladder (D0 1000, D1
1085, ck_6144 1101). The raw win rate is reported alongside because it
is the number the flagship league actually cares about.

### Two deviations from the parent lane, both forced by from-random-init

1. **Field share.** An argmax-mode random-init snapshot is nearly
   passive: the sampling seat beat its own episode-0 clone **64-0** in
   the first chunk, a result with no learnable signal in it. Phase 7b's
   scratch line avoided this by rotating a real external opponent into
   1 chunk in 4; `rl/p10_pilot_pick.py` makes that cadence explicit
   (`--field-share .25`) and lets the Gaussian take over once the
   agent's rating reaches the field.
2. **Nearest-above fallback.** At Elo 46 every Gaussian weight
   underflows, so a flat floor would have made an episode-0 net face
   ck_6144 as often as D0. When all weights underflow the picker takes
   the row closest to the optimism target, which walks the field
   D0 → D1/D1h → champions as the pilot improves.

Between the sparse (2048-episode) measured ratings the self-Elo that
drives PFSP is carried by an ordinary Elo update (K=16) on each
64-episode chunk result against the picked opponent's rating, and
re-anchored to the measured value at every rating. The games are
already being played, so this is free, and it keeps the ladder from
going flat across 32 chunks.

## Environment note

This session's container came up bare (no XMage checkout, no torch), so
the run rebuilt the full setup from CHECKPOINT-PHASE10.md section 5.
The box has **4 cores**, not the machine the Phase 9 fast path was tuned
on, and concurrency was re-measured on it before the first pilot
started:

| rl-vs-rl concurrency | games/sec |
|---|---|
| 2 | 0.605 |
| **3** | **0.715** |
| 4 | 0.562 |

Two policy servers plus the driver JVM oversubscribe 4 cores at conc4,
so these lanes ran at **conc3**. Budget was set to **4096 episodes per
deck** — the low end of the 4–6k band — because three sequential pilots
at the measured in-lane rate is the session's real constraint.
